figures.finding: No collective agreement or guild rate card sets a Hong Kong actor's pay: production companies hire on short-term contracts, pay follows seniority and performance, and the only agreed minimum the government has reported is a daily wage for daily-rated crew (props, mechanics, floor managers, production assistants) coordinated by the Federation of Hong Kong Film Workers.

value.crewDailyMinimum: agreed between employers and employees under the Federation of Hong Kong Film Workers (2007); amount not published in the reply

figures.applies: Hong Kong film production; government reply to the Legislative Council, 14 November 2007.

sources.said: Generally speaking, production companies will normally employ production staff on short-term contracts when producing a new film.

Generally speaking, film veterans and film workers with better performance receive higher pay. However, for the daily-rated workers (such as props men, mechanics, floor managers, tea service attendants and production assistants), under the co-ordination of the Federation of Hong Kong Film Workers, the employer and employee sides have agreed on the minimum daily wage.
The research team believe that the government should take the lead in urging the industry to introduce standard contracts, promote the culture of signing a full agreement before starting work.

figures.finding: The only statutory floor is the general Statutory Minimum Wage, HK$43.1 an hour from 1 May 2026, which applies to every employee under the Minimum Wage Ordinance (an actor engaged as an employee, not one engaged as a freelancer).

value.basis: Minimum Wage Ordinance (Cap. 608), general, not film-specific

figures.applies: Hong Kong, all employees, from 1 May 2026.

sources.said: The SMW rate is raised to $43.1 per hour with effect from 1 May 2026.
Unless otherwise specified, Minimum Wage Ordinance applies to every employee, his employer and the contract of employment under which he is engaged.

figures.finding: The Hong Kong Performing Artistes Guild, a non-profit founded in 1993 by Jackie Chan, Chow Yun-fat, Maggie Cheung and others, represents more than 900 film and television actors, singers, stage performers and voice actors; it publishes no rate card and no membership fee.

value.name: Hong Kong Performing Artistes Guild (香港演藝人協會)

sources.said: 成立於1993年的香港演藝人協會（HKPAG）為非牟利組織，由香港演藝界知名藝人如成龍、梅艷芳、許冠文、周潤發、張曼玉及眾多演藝界人士發起並參與。目前香港演藝人協會（HKPAG）是香港 900餘名電影、電視演員、歌手、舞台表演者及配音演員的代表。

figures.finding: Hong Kong's market is the territory itself: the government's financing requires at least half of a funded film's below-the-line spend to be in Hong Kong and key cast and crew to be permanent residents.

sources.said: 4.3.7 50% or more of the below-the-line expenditures for the implementation, Production, Completion and Delivery of the Film Project must be expended in Hong Kong.

figures.finding: Chinese is Hong Kong's official language, English also usable officially, by Article 9 of the Basic Law; no primary source found names Cantonese as the language of screen work.

value.basis: Basic Law Art. 9; spoken variety not stated

sources.said: In addition to the Chinese language, English may also be used as an official language by the executive authorities, legislature and judiciary
